question: State the conditions that a company must satisfy under the Companies Act, 2013 before it buys back its own shares.
sources: Companies Act, 2013 - section 68 power to purchase own securities
Companies Act, 2013 - section 69 transfer to capital redemption reserve account

points.label: Sources of funds
points.description: Buy-back may be made only out of free reserves, the securities premium account, or the proceeds of an issue of shares or other specified securities, but not from the proceeds of an earlier issue of the same kind of shares.

points.label: Authority and resolution
points.description: The articles must authorise the buy-back and a special resolution is needed; a Board resolution is enough where the buy-back is ten per cent or less of the total paid-up equity capital and free reserves.

points.label: Size limit
points.description: The buy-back must not exceed twenty-five per cent of the total paid-up capital and free reserves; for equity shares, not more than twenty-five per cent of the paid-up equity capital in a financial year.

points.label: Debt-equity ratio
points.description: After the buy-back, secured and unsecured debts must not be more than twice the paid-up capital and free reserves (unless a higher ratio is prescribed for a class of companies).

points.label: Fully paid shares and gap between offers
points.description: Only fully paid-up shares can be bought back, and no new buy-back offer can be made within one year of the previous one.
points.basis: Companies Act, 2013, section 68(2)(e) and proviso to section 68(2)

points.label: Capital redemption reserve
points.description: When shares are bought back out of free reserves or securities premium, a sum equal to the nominal value of the shares bought back is transferred to the capital redemption reserve account.
